acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p stoa-reader passes; no warn! at that location remains; eprintln + exit(1) present; clippy clean
description:
## What
In crates/reader/src/main.rs, change the existing dev-mode warning (lines ~349-356) from warn! to eprintln! + process::exit(1), matching the signing-key guard pattern.

## Algorithm
1. Read crates/reader/src/main.rs lines 320-370.
2. Find the existing block:
     if config.auth.is_dev_mode() && !is_loopback_addr(&config.listen.addr) {
         warn!('...');
     }
3. Replace with:
     if config.auth.is_dev_mode() && !is_loopback_addr(&config.listen.addr) {
         eprintln!(
             'error: stoa-reader is configured in dev mode (auth.required = false, no users configured) \
but is listening on a non-loopback address ({}). This accepts any password from untrusted \
networks. Either: (1) change listen.addr to 127.0.0.1 for local-only use, or (2) set \
auth.required = true and configure auth.users or auth.credential_file.',
             config.listen.addr
         );
         std::process::exit(1);
     }
4. cargo fmt; cargo clippy clean; cargo test --workspace clean.

## Defensive programming rules
- The error message must be actionable: tell the operator exactly what config to change.
- Do not add any new function; modify the existing inline block only.
- No unwrap().

## Tests
Add to crates/reader/src/config.rs test module (or existing test file):
- test_dev_mode_loopback_ok: config with is_dev_mode()=true and listen.addr='127.0.0.1:1119' should not trigger the guard. This is a unit test of the condition logic — since exit(1) cannot be tested in-process, test the predicate: assert!(is_dev_mode && is_loopback_addr('127.0.0.1:1119') is_loopback).
- test_dev_mode_nonloopback_triggers: config with is_dev_mode()=true and listen.addr='0.0.0.0:1119' — test that the condition evaluates to true (the trigger condition). Oracle: the condition is (is_dev_mode && !is_loopback) which must be true for the exit path.
Note: actual process::exit cannot be tested in-process without a subprocess. The unit tests verify the predicate, not the exit. An integration test (spawning the binary) is deferred to the E2E bead.
title: reader: upgrade dev-mode warn to fatal abort on non-loopback
